newsitem.title: UK: London gold moves sideways, seeks impetus.
newsitem.headline: London gold moves sideways, seeks impetus.

text.p: Precious metals prices drifted in narrow ranges on Wednesday morning in a market seeking impetus to probe new territory, dealers said.
Gold prices moved about a dollar higher in early European trading to a high of $346.60 an ounce, largely on professional business, then drifted back.
"It's fairly quiet. Gold hasn't moved very far this morning, although a few people are friendly for gold to move towards $350," a dealer said.
Gold was fixed at $346.10 an ounce, compared with $345.00 on Tuesday afternoon and $346.00 in the morning.
For the time being, prices appeared wedged in a $345.50-$347.00 range.
But gold's technical indicators were turning higher and several dealers said they expected the metal to extend its technical correction from lows below $340 last week.
On the way up gold was likely to run into resistance at around $347, and then the psychological $350 level, dealers and analysts said.
But further gains might require a bout of short covering generated by heavy-hitting investment funds.
"I think we may have to wait until New York comes in. The funds were big sellers yesterday, and we'll have to wait and see if they're up to any tricks today," a dealer said.
Overall, however, gold was still seen locked within a year-old downtrend, and fresh lows dating back to 1993 were expected to be hit in coming weeks or months.
Silver was very quiet but holding last week's sharp gains.
Prices were last indicated at $5.20/$5.22 an ounce, down three cents from Tuesday's London close.
Platinum and palladium prices were little changed, as the market digested this week's news that delayed talks between Russian suppliers and Japanese consumers might resume in the near future.
Platinum was off $0.70 at $367.50/$368.50, while palladium was unchanged at $134.25/$135.25.
Some Far East traders suggested that the metals might have seen their highs for now and were due for a downside correction.
